topics.title: Exposed Server BMCs Leak IPMI Password Hashes
topics.latest_developments: Researchers reported on July 28, 2026 that 24,650 of 36,872 internet-exposed baseboard management controllers hand out password-derived authentication hashes before login, through a flaw in the IPMI 2.0 handshake built on an authentication protocol introduced in 2004.
topics.summary: An attacker who reaches UDP port 623 on a server's controller asks for a hash and receives one without logging in. The BMC runs beneath the operating system, power-cycling the host, mounting virtual media, opening a remote console, and flashing firmware, where host security tools never watch, so administrators should pull these interfaces off the public internet.

sources.title: 24,650 Internet-Exposed BMCs Disclose IPMI Password Hashes Before Login
Over 24,000 exposed server BMCs leak password hash via decades-old flaw
Exposed BMCs hand out password hashes before login

topics.title: US and Australia Push Critical Infrastructure to Isolate OT
topics.latest_developments: CISA, the Australian Signals Directorate's Australian Cyber Security Centre, the FBI, and international partners released joint guidance called CI Fortify on July 28, 2026 urging critical infrastructure operators to prepare to isolate vital operational technology from all other networks during a cyberattack, while Senator Ron Wyden pressed CISA, OMB, and NIST to purge obsolete VPNs from federal agencies.
topics.summary: The guidance gives critical infrastructure organizations practical steps to segment operational technology and enabling systems so an intruder on the IT side cannot reach the machinery that runs power, water, and manufacturing. Wyden's letter frames aging VPN appliances as a persistent entry point that federal agencies should retire.

sources.title: CI Fortify – Advice for isolating vital systems
CISA shares advice on isolating vital systems during cyberattacks
Outdated VPNs should be purged from federal agencies, senator says

topics.title: Chaos Ransomware Rides Teams Vishing as Phishing Surges
topics.latest_developments: Sophos detailed on July 28, 2026 how Chaos ransomware operators used Microsoft Teams vishing, custom malware, and remote access tools to reach ransomware deployment, and Cisco Talos's Q2 2026 incident-response report tied a surge in intrusions to phishing-based initial access and the weaponization of legitimate remote management tools.
topics.summary: Attackers pose as help-desk staff over Teams voice calls to trick employees into granting remote access, then plant tooling that leads to encryption. Talos found the same pattern across its caseload, with phishing and trusted admin utilities driving the quarter's attack chains.

sources.title: Chaos in Teams vishing
IR Trends Q2 2026: Phishing and weaponized remote management tools drive attack chains

topics.title: Claude Cracks HAWK-256 and Speeds an AES Attack
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic reported on July 28, 2026 that its Claude Mythos Preview model helped derive an end-to-end key-recovery attack against the HAWK-256 post-quantum signature scheme and a 200- to 800-fold speedup for an attack on seven-round AES-128.
topics.summary: The HAWK attack exploits a previously unused symmetry in the lattice under the signature scheme, and Anthropic's released implementation recovers a key in about three hours and 42 minutes on a 96-core server. HAWK-256 is a test scheme, yet the result shows an AI model accelerating genuine cryptanalysis.

sources.title: Claude AI Just Cracked a Post-Quantum Test Scheme and Found a Faster 7-Round AES Attack

topics.title: Tengu Botnet Reboots Linux Devices to Survive Cleanup
topics.latest_developments: Nozomi Networks Labs reported on July 28, 2026 that a new Mirai-derived botnet called Tengu abuses a compromised Linux device's hardware watchdog to trigger a reboot when defenders kill its main process, giving its other persistence mechanisms another chance to relaunch it.
topics.summary: The dropper reaches Nozomi's honeypots through Telnet credential brute force, and the malware supports 25 distributed denial-of-service methods. Operators of internet-facing Linux devices should close Telnet and change default credentials.

sources.title: Tengu Botnet Reboots Compromised Linux Devices When Defenders Kill Its Process

topics.title: Agentic Browser Flaws Reopen Old Web Attacks
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading reported on July 27, 2026 that a class of flaws it calls PleaseFix makes agentic browsers easy to socially engineer and exposes weaknesses in how they handle cross-origin requests, effectively rolling web security back two decades.
topics.summary: Agentic browsers act on a user's behalf across sites, and the PleaseFix pattern lets an attacker plant instructions that the agent follows across origins, bypassing the same-origin protections that guard ordinary browsers. The finding widens the attack surface as AI agents take over routine web tasks.

sources.title: Agentic Browsers Rewind Web Security by 20 years
